title: CSS tooltips and accessible disclosure patterns
learningObjectives: Explain css tooltips and accessible disclosure patterns and its role in modern CSS.
Write valid CSS syntax and predict the computed result.
Choose the technique appropriate to a real interface requirement.
Identify common implementation, accessibility, and browser-support pitfalls.
Test and explain the behaviour using browser developer tools.

understand.concept: A tooltip is a short, non-interactive description associated with a control or item. A CSS-only tooltip can be shown on hover and keyboard focus, but a robust implementation must not rely on hover alone. Use a real focusable control when the trigger is interactive, associate the tooltip text with aria-describedby when appropriate, and ensure the content remains available while the pointer moves between trigger and tooltip. Tooltips should not contain essential actions or complex interactive content; use a disclosure or popover pattern for that. Consider Escape dismissal, touch input, reduced motion, and contrast.
understand.whyItMatters: Tooltips can explain unfamiliar controls, but inaccessible hover-only patterns exclude keyboard and touch users and can hide essential information.
understand.analogy: A tooltip is a brief footnote that appears beside the item it explains.
understand.analogyLimit: A footnote analogy does not capture focus management, screen-reader announcement timing, touch behaviour, or dismissal rules.

explain.narrative: Build a help button whose description appears on hover and focus. Then compare it with a disclosure button for content that includes an action or longer explanation.

practise.guidedTask: Build a short tooltip for a form control that works on hover and keyboard focus. Associate it with the control and test it on a touch device.
practise.independentTask: Decide whether a help pattern should be a tooltip, disclosure, or dialog. Document the decision based on content length, interaction, focus behaviour, and whether the content is essential.
hints: Do not show information only on hover.
Use a disclosure or popover for interactive or lengthy content.
Keep the tooltip itself non-interactive and provide a visible focus indicator.

questions.prompt: Which users are excluded by a hover-only tooltip?
questions.explanation: Hover is not a reliable interaction for keyboard and touch users.

questions.prompt: What is aria-describedby commonly used for in a tooltip pattern?
options: Associating the control with its descriptive text
questions.answer: Associating the control with its descriptive text
questions.explanation: aria-describedby references text that provides additional description.

questions.prompt: What pattern is better for content containing interactive controls?
questions.explanation: Tooltips are intended for brief descriptions, not interactive content.

questions.prompt: Which interaction should be considered for a robust tooltip?
options: Keyboard focus and an appropriate dismissal behaviour
Automatic opening on every page load
questions.answer: Keyboard focus and an appropriate dismissal behaviour
questions.explanation: Accessible tooltips must work beyond pointer hover.

questions.prompt: Should essential instructions exist only in a tooltip?
questions.explanation: Essential information must remain available without relying on a transient tooltip.
